issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Shifts that come late or feel harsh, the engine revving without the car picking up speed, or the car refusing to move in drive or reverse. Most reports come at high mileage.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears internally with age and miles, and old or low fluid speeds that up. Owners of 2003 and 2005 cars report full failures around 145,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color first. If it slips or won't engage, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis. On a car this age a used or rebuilt unit is usually the most sensible fix.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor connector can come loose and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and may not restart. A check engine light may come on before it happens.
issues.why: Engine oil could seep into the crankshaft position sensor's wiring plug because the sensor body was molded badly. Heat then swells and deforms the plug until it lets go, cutting the engine's timing signal. Toyota recalled about 35,000 Echos (06V-266) and replaces the sensor free.
issues.next: Run your VIN on nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Toyota dealer. If the recall was never done, book it right away; a stall in traffic is dangerous.

issues.t: Packed snow can damage the rear brake lines (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near a rear wheel, a soft or low brake pedal, or the brake warning light, usually after driving in deep snow.
issues.why: In repeated stop-and-go driving through deep snow, snow can pack and freeze inside the rear wheel area and rub the rear brake line as the wheel turns, wearing through it. Toyota recalled about 59,000 Echos (02V-268) and replaces the rear brake lines.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you see fluid at a rear wheel or the pedal feels soft, don't drive it; have it towed to a shop.

issues.t: Weak power brake assist in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the car takes longer to stop, mainly right after a cold start with the A/C or other electrical loads on.
issues.why: On 2000 Echos with an automatic, the engine may not make enough intake vacuum for the brake booster under those conditions. Toyota recalled about 42,000 cars (01V-326) and replaced the brake booster and front pads.
issues.next: Confirm with a Toyota dealer that the recall was done. If the pedal still feels hard, have the booster and vacuum hose checked.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder seal can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A dropping brake fluid level, fluid wetness at the back of the master cylinder, or a pedal that sinks or feels spongy.
issues.why: A rubber seal ring at the end of the master cylinder could corrode because of a bad washing step at the factory. Fluid can leak past it or air can get in, which lengthens stopping distances. Toyota recall 04V-455 inspects and replaces the master cylinder and booster as needed.
issues.next: Check for an open recall with your VIN. If the fluid keeps dropping or the pedal sinks, have the brakes checked before driving further.

issues.t: Frozen moisture at the brake vacuum port in winter (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal and less braking help in very cold weather.
issues.why: Moisture from the crankcase ventilation (PCV) port could run toward the brake booster's vacuum port inside the intake manifold and freeze there, cutting brake assist. Recall 00V-256 covered cars in 19 cold-weather states, and dealers modify the port.
issues.next: If your car has lived in a cold state, check that the recall was done. Any car with a hard pedal in winter should be inspected.

issues.t: Check engine light from the EVAP system
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on but the car drives normally. A scan shows an evaporative emissions (EVAP) code.
issues.why: The EVAP system traps fuel vapor from the tank. A loose or worn gas cap, a cracked hose, or a failing charcoal canister or valve lets vapor escape and sets the light. RepairPal lists this as the most-reported Echo problem.
issues.next: Tighten or replace the gas cap first and drive a few days. If the light returns, have a shop smoke-test the EVAP system to find the leak.

issues.t: Sluggish acceleration from a dirty airflow sensor
issues.sym: The car feels weak or hesitant when you press the gas, idles unevenly, or gets worse mileage. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The mass airflow (MAF) sensor measures air going into the engine. Over many miles it gets coated with dirt and oil and misreads, so the engine gets the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check the sensor readings. Cleaning it with MAF cleaner often fixes it; replace it only if cleaning doesn't help.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing ignition coil
issues.sym: Rough running, shaking at idle, hesitation, a flashing or steady check engine light, and misfire codes (P0300-P0304).
issues.why: Each cylinder has its own ignition coil on top of the spark plug. With age and engine heat a coil can crack or weaken and stop firing its cylinder properly.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Swapping coils between cylinders shows whether the misfire moves with the coil. Replace the bad coil and check the spark plugs at the same time.

issues.t: Check engine light for misfire codes on early cars
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with misfire codes (P0300 or a single cylinder) even though the engine may seem to run fine.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletins (EG00900 and 413) for early Echos that could set misfire codes under certain driving conditions, and gave dealers a repair procedure.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Toyota dealer whether the bulletin repair was done. Rule out real misfire causes like a bad coil or plug first.

issues.t: Check engine light for variable valve timing (P1349)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P1349. The engine may idle rough, hesitate or feel down on power. Some owners also hear timing chain rattle.
issues.why: The VVT-i system shifts the cam timing using engine oil pressure. A sticking oil control valve, sludge from skipped oil changes, or a worn timing chain and sprockets can set this code. Toyota issued bulletin 00903 for it.
issues.next: Check that the oil is full and clean. A shop should test the oil control valve and its screen before replacing the timing chain.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor code (P0335) from a weak battery
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0335, sometimes with hard starting, often in cold weather or after slow cranking.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-TT-0010-10 says low battery voltage while cranking can set this code even when the sensor itself is fine.
issues.next: Test the battery and charging system before replacing the crank sensor. On 2001-2002 cars, also check the crank sensor recall.

issues.t: Check engine light for knock sensor (P0325)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0325. The car usually drives normally, though power may dip slightly.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin 03904 covers a knock sensor circuit code on these years. The sensor or its wiring reports a fault to the engine computer.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed and ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin. Check the wiring and connector before replacing the sensor.

issues.t: Check engine light for torque converter lockup (P0741)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0741. You may notice higher revs on the highway or slightly worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch locks the engine to the transmission at cruising speed. Toyota bulletin 02504 covers this code, which points to the lockup solenoid, fluid condition or internal wear.
issues.next: Have the transmission fluid checked and the code diagnosed. Ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin repair before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: A/C compressor stops working
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, or the compressor clutch doesn't click on. You may hear a grinding or rattling noise when the A/C is on before it fails.
issues.why: The compressor wears out or its clutch fails with age, often after a slow refrigerant leak lets it run low on oil.
issues.next: Have the system pressure-checked for leaks. If the compressor itself has failed, the dryer and expansion valve are usually replaced with it.

issues.t: Weak heater and A/C fan or missing fan speeds
issues.sym: Weak airflow from the vents, or the fan only works on some speeds, such as only low and high.
issues.why: Owners of 2004-2005 Echos report a weak blower fan. Losing some fan speeds usually means a failed blower resistor; weak airflow on every setting points to the blower motor or a clogged cabin air filter.
issues.next: Check and replace the cabin filter if the car has one. If speeds are missing, have the blower resistor tested; it is a simple part.

issues.t: Manual transmission pops out of reverse
issues.sym: On manual cars, the shifter jumps out of reverse while backing up, so the car rolls in neutral.
issues.why: Worn shift detents, linkage or internal parts let reverse gear disengage under load.
issues.next: Hold the shifter while reversing until it is fixed and park with the brake set. Have the shift linkage and transmission mounts checked first; internal repair is a bigger job.

issues.t: Surface rust on the floor under the carpet
issues.sym: Rust spots on the floor pan under the carpet, sometimes found when a damp smell leads owners to pull the carpet back.
issues.why: Toyota found that the cabin floor under the carpet could show surface rust and ran a limited service campaign (05020) that added a two-phase floor corrosion protection kit.
issues.next: Lift the carpet and check for rust or damp spots, especially if the carpet is ever wet. Ask a Toyota dealer whether the campaign applies; treat rust before it goes through.

issues.t: Water leaking into the cabin and musty smell
issues.sym: Wet carpet or floor mats, fogged windows, or a musty smell inside the car after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water gets past door, glass or body seals or blocked drains. Toyota bulletin T-SB-0094-21 covers finding the water entry point and cleaning up the musty odor.
issues.next: Find where the water comes in (a shop can water-test the car), fix the seal or drain, and dry the carpet and padding fully to stop mold and floor rust.

issues.t: Roof drip molding coming loose
issues.sym: The trim strip along the roof edge lifts, flaps or whistles at highway speed, or looks bent.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin BO01402 says the roof drip molding can come loose or deform, and gives dealers a repair.
issues.next: Have the molding reattached or replaced before it tears off at speed.

issues.t: Sagging headliner
issues.sym: The roof lining fabric sags or falls down onto your head or blocks the rear-view mirror.
issues.why: The foam backing glue breaks down with heat and age, letting the fabric drop.
issues.next: An upholstery shop can recover the headliner board. Pins or spray glue are only a short-term fix.

issues.t: Creak or tick from the windshield or rear glass
issues.sym: A creak, tick or rattle near the top or bottom of the windshield or the top of the rear window, often over bumps.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-SB-0141-10 traces this noise to the glass's bonded stoppers or the glass shifting slightly in its urethane bead.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or glass shop to follow the bulletin; it is a comfort issue, not a safety one, unless the glass has been replaced poorly.

issues.t: Exhaust flex pipe or muffler leak
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, a rumble or buzz under the car, or a rattle at idle. You may smell exhaust.
issues.why: The braided flex pipe and the muffler rust and crack with age, salt and heat. Exhaust parts are the most-reported repair in TrueDelta's Echo survey.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected on a lift. Fix leaks near the front of the car soon, since fumes can get into the cabin.

issues.t: Clunking from worn control arms or bushings
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a loose or wandering feel, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Rubber bushings in the lower control arms and links wear out with age, letting the parts move more than they should.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Replace worn arms or bushings and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Humming or growling wheel bearing
issues.sym: A hum or growl that rises with speed and may change when you turn left or right.
issues.why: Wheel bearings wear out over time, especially after potholes or water getting past the seal.
issues.next: Have a shop find which wheel is noisy. Replace the bearing soon; a badly worn one can affect steering and braking.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends
issues.sym: Loose or vague steering, a clunk when turning, or the front tires wearing on the edges.
issues.why: The tie rod ends connect the steering rack to the wheels and wear out with miles and rough roads.
issues.next: Have the steering checked for play. Replace worn tie rod ends and get an alignment.

issues.t: Door latch not opening or locking properly
issues.sym: A door that won't open from the inside or outside, won't latch shut, or won't lock.
issues.why: The latch mechanism inside the door wears or sticks with age and dirt. Door latches show up among owner-reported repairs for the Echo.
issues.next: Try lubricating the latch. If it still sticks, have the latch assembly replaced, since a door that doesn't latch can open while driving.
